text.p: Merrill Lynch upgraded Hungarian retail group Fotex to long-term 'buy' from 'accumulate' and to intermediate 'accumulate' from 'neutral', saying Fotex will benefit from an economic upturn.

"The retail environment looks set for a turnaround and management changes are tabled for Q3 1997," analyst Thomas Chadwick said in a company update, adding that Merrill Lynch regarded Fotex as one of the cheapest stocks on the market.

Domestic demand in Hungary looks to escalate towards 1998, Chadwick said, adding that with a GDP growth forecast to reach 3.5 percent next year and four to five percent in 1999, Merrill Lynch anticipated a substantial pick up in consumer activity.
"Fotex, with its broad portfolio of retail outlets, should be a prime beneficiary," he said.
The analyst did not share the opinion of critics who cite management issues as a major negative.
"With management now in control of over 45 percent of the company they have a vested interest in adding shareholder value," Chadwick said.
On Thursday Fotex shares rallied 22 forints to close at 174 forints on the Budapest Stock Exchange.
